sizeReason: Lina is working alone for 12 hours over one weekend, with a free-only budget. A single to-do page fits a one-page plan with two experts. Keep due dates and dark mode for later. The designer can help keep the screen calm, minimal, and easy to use.

parts.summary: Build a calm, minimal to-do page for Lina to use on her laptop while learning JavaScript.
parts.details: Finish this weekend in two days, using free tools. Lina owns all work. Plan 8 hours of tasks and reserve 4 hours for problems: more than the required 30% buffer.

parts.summary: Use HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript with localStorage, the browser’s persistent storage. Free, small, and suited to Lina’s learning goal.
parts.details: Serve the page locally at a fixed address. Use index.html, style.css, core.js and app.js. Keep task rules separate from screen updates and storage. Allow 2 hours for JavaScript learning within the 12-hour weekend.

tasks.title: Learn events, arrays and storage; setup
Build task rules and screen actions

checklist.answer: Lina knows HTML/CSS and some JavaScript; budget 2 learning hours.
One page; drop frameworks, backend services and databases.

Local hosting costs nothing: roughly four local requests/load, zero remote requests. Assume 1,000 short tasks under 1 MiB; localStorage allows 5 MiB. No hosting rows, sleep or bandwidth quotas. Full storage stops saves. [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage_API/Storage_quotas_and_eviction_criteria).
No outside restrictions.
Diagram above: actions change task records, then save and redraw.
One stored task array: id, text, done. No automatic backup; document copying stored data to a file.
Single-user actions update immediately; no polling needed.
Small personal project.
Pure add/toggle/delete functions return arrays; app.js handles clicks, IDs, storage and rendering.
Split before 400 lines; reuse helpers; comments explain only why.
First test add/toggle/delete and blank input; then reload, browser restart and failed saves.

README: install Python 3 if needed, run python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1; open localhost:8000. Target under 15 minutes. Keep this address: file-opening storage is unreliable. [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage).
Brief fits. Keep due dates and dark mode deferred; these tasks leave 5 hours for styling and contingency.

merge.title: Lina’s Quiet To-Do

summaries.summary: Build a calm, minimal task page for Lina’s laptop this weekend while she learns JavaScript.
Day one: add, tick off, delete and keep tasks after reopening; due dates and dark mode wait.
Choose HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript: free and direct learning, but requires wiring actions; React offers reusable screen pieces but adds too much learning for Lina’s 12 hours.
Lina owns block 1: 8 planned hours, including learning, plus 4 hours for problems—above the required 30% buffer.
Use localStorage in the same browser at a fixed local address; saved tasks can disappear if browser data is cleared.

Save and restore tasks and ticks; show saving errors (1.25h).
Demonstrate all essentials and review progress (0.5h).
Check rules, keyboard use, reload and reopening; fix issues; write startup steps (2h).
